description: Wires the architecture regression gauntlet + the 7 focused architecture/intake/repair safety test files into .github/workflows/test.yml as a new `arch-gauntlet` job. The job runs on ubuntu-latest with Python 3.11, Rust stable, Go 1.21, and just installed. It invokes the gauntlet in --strict mode, runs the focused test files, re-validates the evidence index, and uploads the gauntlet JSON as a 30-day artifact. Closes the gap-to-100 audit's hidden-assumption #9 (Linux/macOS witness data missing for the portability + safety invariants).
purpose: Rung 7 of the post-audit Claude-lane sequence. With MUST_MIGRATE=0 and BLOCKED_UNSAFE=0 from rung 6, the architecture lane is at the cleanest possible baseline for CI witness wiring. Going forward, every push/PR that touches scripts/, tests/, locks/, or the workflow itself runs the gauntlet on Ubuntu and proves the invariants survive an environment Ryan has never personally observed.
invariants: The arch-gauntlet job is present in .github/workflows/test.yml (workflow_present asserted by test_workflow_defines_arch_gauntlet_job).
The job pins python-version: "3.11" so it runs against the same interpreter version the locks were issued against.
The job runs on ubuntu-latest — Linux witness for portability and safety invariants.
The gauntlet is invoked with --strict so any non-PASSED rollup fails CI (exit 1).
The job invokes `determinex evidence validate` so evidence integrity is re-verified in CI on every run.
The job invokes every required focused test file (7 total — pinned in REQUIRED_FOCUSED_TESTS and tested per file).
DETERMINEX_NO_CORPUS_WRITE=1 set in job env — any corpus write attempt during the gauntlet raises rather than silently mutating CI state.
The gauntlet JSON report is uploaded as an artifact (retention 30 days, if: always).
No `docker pull` / `docker run` / `podman pull` / `podman run` in the job — strictly per directive.
No T:/ drive letter reference in the job — environment portability is the whole point.
No ProgramBench invocations in the job (no pb_*, determinex_programbench*, programbench eval, tests/corpus/programbench/).
No unpinned `pip install` lines — only `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pip install -e .[dev]`, or `pip install -e .` permitted.

The lock manifest's pinned focused_tests_invoked list matches REQUIRED_FOCUSED_TESTS in the test module AND the workflow file (three-way drift caught by test_lock_manifest_lists_all_required_focused_tests).
The lock manifest's pinned python_version is exactly '3.11'.
The lock manifest's pinned runs_on is exactly 'ubuntu-latest'.
Workflow read does not mutate signed evidence.
remaining_gaps: 121 UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_REVIEW sites in the parallel execution audit remain unchanged. The next Claude rung (SCRIPT_HELPER_EXECUTION_CLASSIFICATION_SWEEP_LOCK_001) is the right venue to triage them.

CI does not yet run macOS — only ubuntu-latest. Adding a matrix on (windows-latest, macos-latest) would be a follow-up but is not load-bearing because the gauntlet's PATH_PORTABILITY check already proves no drive-letter dependency.

The arch-gauntlet job duplicates a few install steps (pip + cargo + go + just) that the existing per-language jobs also do. Sharing setup via a composite action is a future cleanup, not a correctness issue.

The focused-test list is pinned in three places (REQUIRED_FOCUSED_TESTS in the test module, focused_tests_invoked in this lock manifest, and the YAML pytest invocation in the workflow). Drift between any two is caught by tests; consolidating to a single source of truth is a future cleanup.

CI does not pin the gauntlet's check count (currently 17). If a future rung adds a check, the gauntlet's own STATUS_TOKENS test catches it, but adding a count assertion in this lock would tighten the contract further.
